messages:
maya: heads-up: since ~02:03 UTC we've seen TLS handshakes fail intermittently in eu-central when we flipped the minimum-cipher policy to tls13-only. errors look like \"handshake: keystore unwrap failed\" from ingress proxies. any RBAC/keystore changes recently?

ben: I pushed the cipher-hardening change last night (tls13-only) and also applied the keystore-role prune early this morning. both were small rollouts.

igor: logs: proxy -> keystore show AccessDenied on KMS Decrypt for alias/edge-priv-eu-central. sample id: 3c7a11. proxy log snippet below.

maya: paste?

igor: ```
2026-06-11T02:03:12Z ingress-eu-2 INFO handshake failed err=keystore: unwrap denied key=alias/edge-priv-eu-central req=3c7a11 proto=TLS1.3
kms: AccessDenied: user arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/keystore-cleanup is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt
```

ben: ugh. the keystore-cleanup rename was supposed to be additive. key-policy updater ran but flagged a propagation warning for eu-central and moved on. maybe propagation lag + cipher change increased handshake frequency so failures are visible now.

oncall: paging SRE. this is affecting a small subset of tenants behind edge hosts in eu-central (latency spikes + 0.6% failed handshakes).

maya: immediate options: revert cipher-hardening (sleepy but lowers SLO), re-add old keystore principal to key policy (fast), revert RBAC rename (slow). which is fastest with least blast radius?

igor: re-adding principal to key-policy for affected alias is fastest; we can also add a tag-based allow for principals with Tag service=keystore to avoid ARN fragility.

deploy-bot: rbac/keystore-prune rollout completed 2026-06-11T00:45:00Z in eu-central and ap-south. keypolicy-updater reported warnings for aliases: alias/edge-priv-eu-central (propagation-warning).

ben: i'm going to patch key policy to include both: old role arn and a temporary tag-based condition. will apply to alias/edge-priv-eu-central now.

igor: policy snippet i'm about to apply: 
```json
{"Statement":"Allow","Principal":"*","Action":"kms:Decrypt","Condition":{"StringEquals":{"aws:PrincipalTag/service":"keystore"}}}
```

maya: after patch, run canary decrypt and then a TLS probe to simulate handshakes to observe restored resumption behavior.

igor: patch applied at 02:12:10Z. waiting 30s for propagation.

ben: canary in eu-central: 
```
curl -k -H "x-req-id: canary-tls-01" https://keystore.eu-central.internal/decrypt -d '{"key":"alias/edge-priv-eu-central","cipher":"..."}'
```

igor: canary succeeded req=canary-tls-01 status=200 decrypt_ms=42. running TLS probe across 10 ingress nodes now.

deploy-bot: tls-probe: 10/10 nodes reported successful TLS1.3 handshakes and resumption. failure rate dropped to baseline.

oncall: scheduling cert refresh for impacted hosts and will monitor 1h. creating alert: KEYSERVICE.UNWRAP_DENIED > 0.5% for 5m => page.

maya: why did keypolicy-updater skip alias/edge-priv-eu-central? follow-ups needed.

igor: keypolicy-updater logs show a transient 500 from the keymanagement API during the region sweep; updater logged a warning and continued. no retry for that alias. we should make updater fail the deploy on any non-zero warnings for critical aliases.

ben: follow-ups I'm putting on my list:
- make keypolicy-updater fail-fast on propagation warnings for any alias used by ingress/edge keystore
- add preflight: diff role ARNs vs key policy principals for all keystore aliases before RBAC prune
- add a canary step where we run a TLS probe that triggers a decrypt (simulate handshake) in the target region before toggling cipher policy
- increase CloudTrail delivery alerting; audit-bot noticed some denies had missing principal fields during the window (AUD-2026-2112)

audit-bot: created audit ticket AUD-2026-2112: partial CloudTrail delivery found for 02:00-02:15 UTC, some kms:Decrypt denies missing principal attribute. cloudinfra engaged.

oncall: decision: keep cipher-hardening enabled; keep temporary tag-based allow in key policy for 48h; revert RBAC prune after postmortem if necessary.

maya: assigning postmortem owner: maya. initial SLA impact: 19m of elevated handshake latency / 0.6% failed handshakes affecting edge tenants in eu-central. I'll link incident doc here when created. thanks team. :thumbsup:
